module.label: Place Order
module.title: Place Order
module.summary: Place an internet package order for a selected corporate customer, from customer context and plan search through service configuration, fulfilment, payment and final order result.

nodes.title: Physical device fulfilment?
nodes.subtitle: Branch by product, service and selected device

edges.label: SIM, eSIM, top-up or assigned device

flows.title: Start order and establish customer context
flows.evidence: AS-IS traced in active Place Order implementation
flows.trigger: Select Place Order, open /admin/placeorder, or arrive from Support with a customer prefill.
flows.summary: Restore the operator's assigned source, allow only urwifi operators to change it, and select the customer that every later plan, device, charge and payment request must use.
preconditions: The operator is authenticated and has access to Place Order.
The active login contains a source and corporate operator identity.
A support-assisted entry may have written cs_placeorder_prefill to sessionStorage.
flows.outcome: A verified userProfile, userId and source are stored in the working order and an end-user token is requested.

steps.title: Initialize order state
steps.detail: Prefer Support prefill, otherwise restore po_order_state, otherwise use the logged-in customer context when available.

steps.title: Logged-in source is urwifi?
steps.detail: Show the Source dropdown only when the authenticated operator's source is urwifi; otherwise keep the assigned source internally and hide the selector.

steps.title: Choose customer
steps.detail: An urwifi operator may first choose a source. Every operator then types at least three valid characters or selects a returned customer.

steps.title: Search scoped users
steps.detail: Debounce for 500 ms and request matching Jane users with source, group_id and corp_id.

steps.title: Exact customer found?
steps.detail: Only an exact normalized userId match becomes the active userProfile.

steps.title: Persist safe context
steps.detail: Write source, user profile, user ID, device type, travel details and promo code to po_order_state.

steps.title: Enable package search
steps.detail: The customer is ready and the end-user token lookup runs for the selected source.

branches.label: urwifi operator
branches.detail: Show the Source dropdown and allow selection from the operator's permitted sources.

branches.label: Other source
branches.detail: Hide the Source dropdown and use the authenticated operator's assigned source for customer search and downstream requests.

branches.label: Support prefill
branches.detail: Use cs_placeorder_prefill and mirror its customer context into po_order_state.

branches.label: Saved order context
branches.detail: Restore the persisted subset when no newer support prefill exists.

branches.label: No exact user
branches.detail: Keep package search disabled and show that the user profile does not exist.

branches.label: Source changes
branches.detail: Clear customer, travel, promo and deposit data to prevent cross-source ordering.

apis.name: getAllJaneUsers
apis.purpose: Find customers within the operator's source and corporate scope.

rules.text: Every order must be bound to one verified customer and one approved source before package selection; only an authenticated urwifi operator may see and use the Source dropdown.
Changing source invalidates previously selected customer, travel and promotional context.
Support prefill must never bypass the same customer and authorization checks used by direct entry.

gaps.text: cs_placeorder_prefill is read but not removed in the active Rent flow, so stale support context can be replayed on a later visit.
The component performs a client-side login redirect, but route-level authorization and backend Place Order permission enforcement are not demonstrated here.

acceptance.text: An unauthenticated or unauthorized operator cannot open the route or retrieve customer data.
Package search stays disabled until an exact customer profile is selected.

The Source dropdown is visible only when the authenticated operator source is urwifi; all other operators keep their assigned source without a selector, and any permitted source change clears customer-specific order state.
A consumed support prefill is cleared or explicitly marked consumed.

flows.title: Search and select an internet package
flows.trigger: A customer is selected and the operator chooses destination, dates, product type and optional promo code.
flows.summary: Load eligible partner or local plans for the customer and destination, validate promotions, filter the result and select one package.
preconditions: A verified customer profile and source exist.
A travel country is selected.
The plan search is not already running.
flows.outcome: The selected package is stored in order.package and navigation continues to Cart Service.

steps.title: Enter trip criteria
steps.detail: Choose destination, optional date range for SIM/eSIM, required dates for Pocket WiFi, product type and optional promo code.

steps.title: Partner plan group?
steps.detail: Eligible partner groups load partner plans; other operators use local plans scoped by user, destination and source.

steps.title: Promo supplied?
steps.detail: Load promo details and, for non-global promos, validate the selected country before plan search.

steps.title: Load eligible plans
steps.detail: Request plans with origin, destination, customer, source and partner context.

steps.title: Filter plans
steps.detail: Filter by Pocket WiFi, SIM or eSIM, plan category, plan name or code, and load more results.

steps.title: Select package
steps.detail: Store the package; the Rent effect navigates to /admin/placeorder/pocketwificartservice.

branches.label: Global promo
branches.detail: Proceed directly to the plan search using the promo code.

branches.label: Country-restricted promo
branches.detail: Continue only when validatePromoCountry marks the selected country eligible.

branches.label: No plans
branches.detail: Show a distinct no-packages result and allow the operator to change criteria.

branches.label: API failure
branches.detail: Stop the loading state and surface the returned error message.

apis.name: localPlans
apis.purpose: Load destination-eligible plans for the selected customer.

apis.name: validatePromoCountry
apis.purpose: Validate a non-global promo against the selected destination.

errorResponse.message: Promo is not valid for this country

rules.text: Plan eligibility must use the selected customer's identity, origin, destination, source and approved partner scope.
A country-restricted promo cannot affect charges until the destination validation succeeds.
Pocket WiFi requires valid travel dates before service configuration can complete; SIM/eSIM dates may be optional at search time.

gaps.text: Initial priority-plan loading can show plans before destination criteria are submitted; the eligibility contract between priority plans and later local-plan search should be explicit.
A hard-coded operator exception for aziz@dealer.com changes partner scoping and should be replaced with a documented policy or permission.

acceptance.text: Search cannot run without a verified customer and destination.
Only plans eligible for the chosen customer, source and destination are selectable.
An invalid promo cannot be applied or carried into pricing.
Selecting a package moves exactly once to Cart Service with the chosen plan preserved.

flows.title: Configure service, variation and device
flows.summary: Load plan variations and customer devices, then choose service type, data size, duration, dates, quantity and an existing device when the flow requires one.
preconditions: A package with planCode and product type is stored in the Redux cart.
The selected customer and source are still available.
Travel details exist when the product requires them.
flows.outcome: A valid variation and optional selectedDevice are stored in orderData and the operator can continue to Plan Summary.

steps.title: Load variations
steps.detail: Request getPlanVariations using planCode and product type for Pocket WiFi.

steps.title: Load customer devices
steps.detail: Request devices using userId, appUserId and source.

steps.title: Group service choices
steps.detail: Normalize variations into rent, buy, top-up, SIM and eSIM service groups with data sizes and durations.

steps.title: Choose service configuration
steps.detail: Select service type, data size, duration, quantity and travel dates as required.

steps.title: Existing device required?
steps.detail: Top-up requires a compatible customer device; lookup by device ID also warns when ownership differs.

steps.title: Store cart configuration
steps.detail: Write variation and selectedDevice into the shared order object and enable Next only when required data is complete.

branches.label: SIM/eSIM purchase
branches.detail: A selected variation is sufficient; travel details are normalized to today's date after selection.

branches.label: Top-up
branches.detail: Require a compatible device and an available top-up variation.

branches.label: Different owner
branches.detail: Allow continuation but generate a new order_id and show a device-ownership warning.

branches.label: No services
branches.detail: Show the no-services state and keep Next disabled.

apis.name: getPlanVariations
apis.purpose: Load service variations for the selected plan.

apis.name: getDevices
apis.purpose: Load devices belonging to the selected customer for top-up or plan assignment.

rules.text: The selected variation must belong to the selected plan and match the intended product and service type.
Top-up requires a compatible device and available variation for that device type and provider.
Pocket WiFi Next remains disabled until every travel leg has location and required dates.

gaps.text: A device that belongs to another user is allowed to proceed after only a warning; the approved ownership and reassignment policy is not defined.
Directly refreshing a later route can leave Redux orderData incomplete because the persisted po_order_state excludes package, variation, selected device, delivery and payment data.

acceptance.text: Next remains disabled until the selected service has a valid variation and all product-specific requirements.
Top-up cannot continue with an incompatible or unavailable device variation.
A later-step refresh recovers the complete order safely or returns the operator to the earliest valid step.
Cross-user device use follows an explicit authorization rule and creates an auditable event.

flows.title: Resolve payment gateway and calculate charges
flows.trigger: Continue from Cart Service with a valid variation.
flows.summary: Resolve the customer's payment gateway, calculate either purchase-order or selected-device plan charges, and show the authoritative total before fulfilment.
preconditions: The order contains customer, package, variation and travel details.
A selectedDevice is present only for a plan/top-up flow.
The backend can resolve a payment gateway for the customer.
flows.outcome: pgwType, amount and any discount are stored; the flow branches to fulfilment or directly to Order Summary.

steps.title: Resolve gateway
steps.detail: Request the customer's payment gateway using encrypted userId and appUserId data.

steps.title: Selected device present?
steps.detail: Use plan charges for an assigned device; otherwise use order charges for a new purchase or rental.

steps.title: Calculate charges
steps.detail: Send plan, package, variation, travel, promo, source and customer fields to the appropriate charge endpoint.

steps.title: Store pricing
steps.detail: Persist authoritative charges and discount in orderData.

steps.title: Review summary
steps.detail: Check product type, data, duration, device or quantity, promo and total.

steps.title: Fulfilment required?
steps.detail: New Pocket WiFi without a selected device goes to Shipping Option; other products and assigned-device flows go to Order Summary.

branches.label: Assigned device
branches.detail: POST plan/charges and bypass physical fulfilment.

branches.label: New Pocket WiFi
branches.detail: POST order/charges, then select fulfilment unless default pickup is explicitly chosen.

branches.label: Skip shipping
branches.detail: Set the fixed Emerald Hill office as self pickup with zero shipping charge and continue to Order Summary.

branches.label: Pricing failure
branches.detail: Show an error state and do not allow confirmation with an unknown total.

apis.name: getPaymentGateway
apis.purpose: Resolve the payment gateway configured for the selected customer.

apis.name: calculateOrderCharges
apis.purpose: Calculate charges when no existing device is selected.

rules.text: The backend-calculated amount is authoritative; the browser must not calculate or override the payable total.
The charge request and final order request must describe the same customer, plan, variation, quantity, travel details and promo.
Physical fulfilment applies only where the selected product and service require delivery or pickup.

gaps.text: The charge hook does not list the complete order configuration in its callback dependencies, so changes beyond pgw or selectedDevice may not automatically trigger recalculation.
Skip Shipping applies one hard-coded office location; availability by customer origin, product and operating hours is not validated in this step.

acceptance.text: The plan summary never displays a confirmable total until the gateway and charge calls succeed.
Any price-affecting change causes charges to be recalculated before confirmation.
The fulfilment branch matches product type, service type and selected-device state.
Default pickup is available only when the fixed location is valid for the order.

flows.title: Choose shipping or self pickup
flows.trigger: A new physical Pocket WiFi order continues from Plan Summary.
flows.summary: Load available fulfilment methods, then route self pickup to location selection or store a delivery method and address for final review.
preconditions: The order needs physical fulfilment.
The customer profile contains origin, userId and appUserId.
Plan charges have already been calculated.
flows.outcome: The order contains either delivery details or proceeds to the Self Pickup flow.

steps.title: Load shipping rates
steps.detail: Request available methods with customer country, userId, appUserId and source.

steps.title: Normalize options
steps.detail: Put self pickup first and exclude it for buy-device variations.

steps.title: Select fulfilment
steps.detail: Choose self pickup or an available paid/free shipping method.

steps.title: Self pickup?
steps.detail: Navigate to pickup-location selection without requiring an address.

steps.title: Select delivery address
steps.detail: For non-self shipping, select a saved address before Next is enabled.

steps.title: Store delivery
steps.detail: Persist shipping type, address ID/data, currency and rate, then open Order Summary.

branches.label: Self pickup
branches.detail: Continue to PO-F06 and choose an active pickup location.

branches.label: Delivery
branches.detail: Require an address and save the authoritative shipping rate.

branches.label: Buy device
branches.detail: Filter self pickup from the returned methods.

branches.label: No methods
branches.detail: Show the empty state and prevent progress.

apis.name: getShippingRate
apis.purpose: Load fulfilment options and shipping rates for the customer origin.

rules.text: Non-self fulfilment requires a valid address belonging to the selected customer.
The shipping rate and currency stored on the order must match the selected backend option.
Buy-device flows may not use self pickup under the current implementation rule.

gaps.text: The reason self pickup is excluded for buy-device flows is encoded in the UI but not expressed as an authoritative backend rule.
Shipping-rate failure is presented as an empty options state, so operators cannot distinguish unavailable fulfilment from a technical error.

acceptance.text: Only backend-returned fulfilment options can be selected.
A delivery method cannot continue without a valid selected customer address.
Self pickup never carries a delivery address or delivery charge.
Technical rate failures are distinguishable from a valid no-options result and can be retried.

flows.title: Select a self-pickup location
flows.trigger: Choose self pickup from Shipping Option.
flows.summary: Load active pickup locations, filter them by country, select one location and store it as zero-delivery-charge fulfilment.
preconditions: Self pickup is an allowed shipping option for the order.
The selected customer has userId and appUserId.
Pickup locations are available from the backend.
flows.outcome: delivery.shippingType is self and delivery.location contains the selected active pickup location.

steps.title: Load all pickup locations
steps.detail: Request locations with cityId 0, simEnabled false and the selected customer identifiers.

steps.title: Filter active locations
steps.detail: Keep locations whose active flag is 1 and derive a unique country list.

steps.title: Choose country
steps.detail: Select the pickup country; reload locations for that country.

steps.title: Choose location
steps.detail: Review address and operating details and choose one location.

steps.title: Both selections present?
steps.detail: Block Next until country and location are selected.

steps.title: Store pickup
steps.detail: Save country, location and shippingType self, then navigate to Order Summary.

branches.label: Origin match
branches.detail: The implementation attempts to preselect a location matching the customer's origin.

branches.label: Country changed
branches.detail: Clear the old location and request the new country's locations.

branches.label: No active locations
branches.detail: Keep Next disabled and explain that no pickup location is available.

branches.label: Load failure
branches.detail: Show an error and preserve the ability to go back to fulfilment selection.

apis.name: getPickupLocations
apis.purpose: Load active pickup locations, optionally filtered by country.

rules.text: Only active pickup locations returned for the selected country may be attached to the order.
Self pickup has zero shipping charge unless the backend explicitly returns a pickup fee.
Changing country invalidates the previously selected location.

gaps.text: Initial origin matching sets selectedLocation but does not set selectedCountry, while form validation requires both; the apparent auto-selection cannot continue.
Pickup API failures use browser alert messages instead of an inline, retryable state.

acceptance.text: Origin auto-selection sets a consistent country and location pair.
Changing country always clears a location from the previous country.
Only an active location in the selected country can be saved.
A failed location request shows an inline Retry action without losing the order.

flows.title: Review order and select payment
flows.trigger: Arrive at Order Summary after pricing and any required fulfilment selection.
flows.summary: Review the full customer, plan, travel, device, fulfilment and total context, select an eligible payment card, and optionally suppress charges when permitted.
preconditions: The order has authoritative charges and payment gateway type.
Required physical fulfilment data exists.
The selected customer identity remains unchanged.
flows.outcome: The operator has reviewed a coherent order and selected a payment path ready for submission.

steps.title: Load payment cards
steps.detail: Request encrypted customer cards and keep supported 2c2p and corporate-card entries.

steps.title: Build review summary
steps.detail: Show user, source, destination, dates, plan, variation, quantity/device, promo, fulfilment and total payable.

steps.title: Select payment
steps.detail: Choose a supported saved card or corporate card.

steps.title: Suppress charges allowed?
steps.detail: The current userProfile supCharges value initializes an optional suppression path.

steps.title: Confirm accuracy
steps.detail: Review the final data before Place Order starts payment and submission.

steps.title: Ready to submit
steps.detail: paymentCard, total and order configuration are ready for PO-F08.

branches.label: 2c2p card
branches.detail: Create a payment session before placing the order.

branches.label: Corporate card
branches.detail: Use pgw crpc and the corporate-card invoice marker.

branches.label: Suppress charges
branches.detail: Skip payment session and place the order with supCharges true.

branches.label: Adyen
branches.detail: The page states that Adyen is currently unavailable for this service.

apis.name: getUserCardsEnc
apis.purpose: Load encrypted saved payment methods for the selected customer.

successResponse.data: <encrypted card array containing cardId and pgw>

rules.text: The final review must match the exact data that will be sent in the order request.
Suppress Charges and corporate-card payment require explicit operator permission and an audit record.
Only payment methods supported by the resolved gateway may be selected.

gaps.text: The UI exposes charge suppression based on userProfile.supCharges; server-side authorization for this financially sensitive action is not demonstrated in the reviewed flow.
Adyen can be resolved as pgwType but the summary declares it unavailable, leaving affected customers without an in-flow recovery path.

acceptance.text: The displayed final summary and submission payload agree on all price- and fulfilment-affecting fields.
Unsupported payment methods cannot be selected or submitted.
Charge suppression is enforced by backend permission and recorded in the order audit trail.
An unavailable gateway provides a clear alternative or stops before Place Order is enabled.

flows.title: Create payment session and place the order
flows.actor: Corporate Portal Operator and Yoowifi order services
flows.trigger: Select Place Order from the reviewed Order Summary.
flows.summary: Create a payment session when required, submit the correct purchase or plan-order payload, then present one unambiguous success or failure result.
preconditions: The final review is complete and payment path is valid.
The order amount and fulfilment data are current.
The operator has not already submitted this order.
flows.outcome: A successful response returns an order ID; a failure preserves the order for safe correction or retry.

steps.title: Place order
steps.detail: Open a blocking loading modal and prevent another submission.

steps.title: Payment session required?
steps.detail: Corporate card and authorized charge suppression skip the external payment-session call.

steps.title: Create payment session
steps.detail: Encrypt customer, amount, card, currency and return URL; store the returned invoiceNo.

steps.title: Top-up service?
steps.detail: Submit /order/plan for serviceType T; otherwise submit /order for purchase/rental.

steps.title: Place authoritative order
steps.detail: Send customer, plan, variation, dates, promo, payment, quantity/device and fulfilment fields.

steps.title: Show final result
steps.detail: Display success with orderId or an error message; closing success returns to Internet Packages.

branches.label: Payment session fails
branches.detail: Show a payment initialization error and do not call the order endpoint.

branches.label: Purchase or rental
branches.detail: POST /yw-services/api/order with fulfilment fields when applicable.

branches.label: Top-up or assigned plan
branches.detail: POST /yw-services/api/order/plan with device and order identifiers.

branches.label: Order succeeds
branches.detail: Show returned order ID, then return to the package step when the modal closes.

branches.label: Order fails
branches.detail: Keep the order available and show either the backend message or a network error.

apis.name: createPaymentSession
apis.purpose: Create the invoice/payment session required before a chargeable order.

apis.name: placeOrder
apis.purpose: Create a new purchase or rental order.

successResponse.message: Your order has been placed successfully

rules.text: The order endpoint must be selected from the final service type, not from browser route history.
A repeated click or retry must not create a duplicate order or duplicate charge.
Success is recognized only from an explicit successful backend result with an order identifier.
Failed submission must preserve enough state for a safe retry without re-entering the full order.

gaps.text: No explicit idempotency key or duplicate-order protection is visible across payment-session creation and final order submission.
Closing a successful result navigates to Internet Packages without explicitly clearing Redux cart data or po_order_state, which can carry stale values into the next order.
Network failure uses a generic message and does not distinguish an order that failed from one whose response was lost after backend creation.

acceptance.text: Place Order is disabled immediately after the first click and remains blocked until a terminal response.
One logical order produces at most one charge and one backend order across retries.
An ambiguous network result can be reconciled by idempotency key or order-status lookup before retry.
Success clears all completed-order state before starting another order.
Failure keeps the reviewed order intact and exposes a safe Retry action.
